q: 1. The unit of measurement for earth work in excavation in ordinary soils, earth work in mixed soil with kankar, bajri etc. when depth of excavation does not exceed 30 cm, is
explain: For shallow excavations (surface excavation) where the depth does not exceed 30 cm, the work is measured in area (sq. m.) rather than volume.

q: 2. *The unit of measurement for wood work in door and window frame, rafters, beams, roof trusses etc. is
explain: Structural woodwork for frames and beams is measured by volume (cubic meters), whereas shutters are often measured by area.

q: 3. *The unit of measurement for electric wiring or electrification light, fan plug points is
explain: Internal electrical wiring is estimated by the number of 'points' (light points, fan points, etc.).

q: 4. The volume of sand a normal truck can carry per trip is approximately
explain: A standard truck used for local material transport typically carries about 3-5 m3 of sand per trip, as per common estimating norms.

q: 5. *For electric wiring such as fan, light, plug etc, the estimate is made in terms of
options: total load at main in kw
total length of wiring in meters
explain: While individual points are counted, the overall estimate for the system often considers the total load in kilowatts for capacity planning.

q: 6. *The quantity of soiling is obtained in
explain: Soling (the layer of stones under a foundation or floor) is typically measured by area for a specified thickness.

q: 7. The quantity of honey-comb walls are worked out in
explain: Honey-comb brickwork, where openings are left in the wall, is measured in square meters.

q: 8. The measurement of steel grills is taken in term of
explain: Steel fabrications like grills are paid for based on their total weight.

q: 9. The unit of measurement of marble skirting is
explain: Skirting is a long, thin strip of work along the base of walls, so it is measured by its running length, i.e., per metre.

q: 10. Measurement of railing of staircase
explain: Handrails and railings are measured along their length in running meters.

q: 11. The unit of measurement of iron hole fast is
explain: A hold fast (iron anchor embedded in masonry to fix door/window frames) is a small metal item measured and paid for by weight, in kg.

q: 12. The unit of brick work having 1/2 brick thick is
explain: A 1/2 brick thick wall is measured in square meters.

q: 13. The volume of cement in one bag is
explain: One bag of cement (50 kg) occupies a volume of approximately 0.035 m³, based on cement's bulk density (~1440 kg/m³).

q: 14. In the estimation of plastering surface the deductions are not made for
explain: In plastering measurements, no deductions are made for small features like beam ends, rafter ends, or openings up to 0.5 m2, since these are considered negligible.

q: 15. The unit of measurement of mass, voluminous and thick work like E/W, B/W, etc is
explain: Bulky, mass items such as earthwork (E/W) and brick work (B/W) in thick sections are measured by volume, m³, since all three dimensions are significant.

q: 16. The weight of cement in one bag is
explain: The standard weight of a bag of ordinary Portland cement, as commercially packaged, is 50 kg.

q: 17. During calculation of RCC, the amount of steel deducted is
explain: In RCC volume calculation, no deduction is normally made for the volume occupied by reinforcement steel embedded in the concrete (0% deduction) since it is negligible.

q: 18. For 100 sq. m cement concrete (1:2:4) 4 cm thick floor, quantity cement required, is
explain: Using the standard cement content formula (dry volume factor 1.64, cement ratio 1/7) applied to the floor volume (100 x 0.04 m), the cement quantity works out to 0.94 m3.

q: 19. Approximate weight of 1 cubic metre of sand is
explain: The typical bulk density of sand used in estimation is approximately 1600 kg per cubic metre.

q: 20. The unit of payment for excavation in trenches for pipes, cables etc. upto 1.5 m depth in ordinary rock/ hard rock is in
explain: Trench excavation for pipes/cables of a standard fixed width is conveniently measured by its running length in meters rather than volume.

q: 21. The expected out turn of brick work in cement mortar (1:6) in foundation and plinth per mason per day (as per MOPIT norms), is
explain: The standard daily output (out-turn) for a mason doing brickwork in the foundation/plinth is 0.83 cubic meters.

q: 22. The quantity of thermoplastic paint for 400 m2 on smooth road surface (as per MOPIT norms), is
explain: MOPIT norms state that 930 liters of thermoplastic paint are needed for a 400m2 smooth road surface.

q: 23. *Brick walls are measured in m2 if the thickness of wall is
explain: Half-brick walls (10 cm thick) are measured by area (m2), whereas full-brick walls are measured by volume (m3).

q: 24. When not specified, the volume of steel in RCC work is taken as
explain: When detailed design isn't available, the percentage of reinforcement steel in RCC work is conventionally assumed as 1% to 1.6% of the concrete volume for preliminary estimation.

q: 25. No deductions is made in the masonry for the opening if the area of the opening does not exceed
explain: Small openings up to 0.10 square meters are ignored in masonry volume calculations.

q: 26. While estimating for lintels over openings, if the dimension for bearing is not given, the bearing is usually taken as equal to
options: half the thickness of lintel or 12 cm whichever is higher
thickness of lintel with a minimum of 12 cm
twice the thickness of lintel with a minimum of 12 cm
explain: When the bearing for a lintel is not specified, standard practice is to take it as half the lintel thickness, subject to a minimum of 12 cm, whichever value is greater.

q: 27. The thickness of slabs and beams must be measured to the nearest
explain: Critical structural thicknesses like slabs and beams are measured to a precision of 0.005 meters (5 mm).

q: 28. Indicating works left in excavated trenches to facilitate the measurement of borrow pints are known as
explain: Tell-tale marks/pegs are left in excavated trenches or borrow pits as reference indicators to help verify and measure the quantity of earthwork excavated.

q: 29. The quantity of partition walls and honey-comb walls are worked out in
explain: Thin partition and honeycomb (jali) walls are treated as area-based masonry items and are measured in square metres.

q: 30. The quantity of partition walls and honey-comb walls are worked out in
explain: Being thin walls, partition and honeycomb walls are measured in square meters (area) rather than volume.

q: 31. The unit measurement of RCC works in shelves of jail (thickness and type specified) is
explain: With thickness and type specified, thin RCC shelf slabs are measured on an area basis, in square metres.

q: 32. The RCC work in beam, slab and lintel is measured in
explain: General RCC structural work such as beams, slabs, and lintels (without a fixed specified thickness convention) is measured by volume, in cubic metres.

q: 33. The unit of measurement of welding and soldering of plates is
explain: Welding/soldering work on steel plates is measured based on the weight of the plates involved, conventionally in quintals.

q: 34. 1 Aana equals
explain: 1 Aana, being 1/16th of a Ropani, equals 342.25 sq. ft. (5476 ÷ 16).

q: 35. Working out the exact quantities of various items of work is known as
explain: Quantity Surveying is the professional discipline of calculating materials, labor, and costs for construction projects.

q: 36. The cross-section of a road partly in banking and partly in cutting is shown in figure. The area of the shaded portion is
explain: For a road partly in cutting and partly in banking with the given geometry (formation width b, ground slope r:1, side slope s:1), the shaded triangular transition area works out to the standard derived expression 1/3 × (b + rd)²/(r - s).

q: 37. Berms are provided in canals if these are
options: partly in excavation and partly in embankment
explain: Berms (level strips left between the canal bank and the excavated slope) are provided when the canal section is fully in excavation (cutting), to provide stability and drainage space.

q: 38. The cross-sections for a highway is taken at
options: right angle to the centre line
the starting end points of the curves
explain: Highway cross-sections are taken at right angles to the centre line, at regular intervals of about 30 m, and also at the start/end points of curves, to fully capture the terrain variation.

q: 39. Approximate weight of cubic meter of sand is
explain: Sand has an approximate bulk density of 1600 kg/m3, the standard value used in estimating.

q: 40. In measuring form work no deduction is made for opening upto
explain: In formwork quantity measurement, small openings up to 0.4 m² are considered negligible and are not deducted from the total formwork area.

q: 41. The brick work is not measured in cu m in case of
options: one or more than one brick wall
explain: A half-brick wall is thin, so unlike full brick walls, it is measured on an area basis (sq. m) rather than by volume.

q: 42. Whenever colour washing on a.c. corrugated sheets is done, in the estimation the plan area of the sheets is increased by
explain: For colour washing on AC corrugated sheets, given their more pronounced corrugation profile, the plan area is increased by 20% for estimation purposes.

q: 43. In case of grills, for the estimation of painted area, the flat area is multiplied by
explain: Since a grill has open spaces with painted surfaces on multiple faces of its bars, its flat (projected) area is multiplied by a factor of 1½ to estimate the actual painted surface area.

q: 44. Thickness of plastering is usually
explain: The standard thickness adopted for ordinary wall plastering is 12 mm, unless a special finish requires otherwise.
